papers.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
papers.abstract: Abstract GPT-6-Astra achieves high performance across diverse robotic tasks via in-context learning, yet real-world deployment reveals gaps in demonstration cost, execution time, and practical embodied intelligence.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., π0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

ru.title: Компетентность есть, практический интеллект ещё впереди
ru.desc: В статье исследуется GPT-6-Astra, большая языковая модель (LLM), которая показывает высокие результаты в робототехнических задачах манипуляции и навигации благодаря in-context learning (ICL) без специализированного обучения под каждую задачу. Авторы оценивают модель на 12 бенчмарках и исследуют связку высокоуровневого «System 2» рассуждающего модуля с низкоуровневым контроллером «System 1» (например, π0.5), которая эффективна, но дорога. Эксперименты на 8 конфигурациях роботов выявляют серьёзные проблемы: сбор демонстраций для ICL дорог, а увеличение времени выполнения ради успеха физически затруднительно. Авторы предлагают новый тип embodied-бенчмарков, работающих по «миру» с реальным временем, и делают вывод, что модель достигла уровня embodied-компетентности, но ещё не практического embodied intelligence.

en.title: GPT-6-Astra: Bridging Robotic Competence and Practical Intelligence
en.desc: The paper discusses GPT-6-Astra, a model that excels in various robotic tasks through in-context learning (ICL). Despite its impressive performance in manipulation and navigation, real-world applications reveal challenges such as high demonstration costs and execution times. The study evaluates GPT-6-Astra across multiple benchmarks and highlights the need for improvements in ICL generality and recovery from failures. Ultimately, while GPT-6-Astra shows significant capabilities, it has not yet achieved practical embodied intelligence.

zh.title: GPT-6-Astra：跨越体现能力的门槛
zh.desc: GPT-6-Astra在多种机器人任务中通过上下文学习实现了高性能，但在实际应用中仍存在演示成本、执行时间和实际体现智能的差距。该模型在机器人操作和导航方面表现出色，挑战了为单一任务构建专门模型的传统观念。研究表明，GPT-6-Astra在多个基准测试中表现优异，但在收集演示数据和执行效率方面仍需改进。未来的研究应关注提高上下文学习的通用性、降低成本和执行时间，以及增强物理状态验证和从不可逆失败中恢复的能力。

papers.title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
papers.abstract: Abstract BizBench evaluates long-horizon business agents on intermediate execution validity using real-world payment procedures, revealing that frontier models frequently violate constraints despite achieving partial goal success.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks often emphasize final task success while providing limited assessment of intermediate execution validity. Yet real-world business operations require agents to navigate extensive, potentially outdated or conflicting policies while satisfying critical constraints throughout execution. These requirements are particularly consequential in high-stakes domains such as payments, where intermediate violations can incur financial losses or regulatory consequences regardless of the final outcome. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce BizBench, a multi-turn benchmark grounded in real-world procedures from a leading payments company. Its executable environment integrates 789 knowledge documents and 601 discoverable business tools, with consistent policies, states, and tool behavior. The benchmark comprises 50 tasks involving resource constraints, temporal dependencies, prior commitments, and conflicting or outdated guidance. Each task is validated through reference execution, while deterministic checks assess both goal attainment and execution validity without prescribing a single solution path. Experiments reveal substantial limitations even among frontier models: Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol achieve strict success rates of only 64.0% and 61.3%, respectively. For Qwen3.8-27B, goal attainment reaches 42.0%, but strict success drops to 32.7%, demonstrating how outcome-based evaluation can mask invalid execution. Beyond success rates, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash averages 191.3 tool calls per run, approximately 70% more than reference executions, revealing substantial execution overhead. Overall, BizBench establishes a testbed for evaluating and advancing long-horizon agents beyond task completion, toward reliable and constraint-compliant execution in complex business environments.

ru.title: Успешный итог не гарантирует корректного пути: проверяем агентов по каждому шагу
ru.desc: В статье представлен BizBench — многоходовый бенчмарк для оценки LLM-агентов в длинных бизнес-сценариях, основанный на реальных платёжных процедурах крупной компании. Среда включает 789 документов со знаниями и 601 инструмент, а 50 задач содержат ресурсные ограничения, временные зависимости и противоречивые или устаревшие правила. Авторы показывают, что даже передовые модели часто нарушают ограничения в ходе выполнения, и что оценка только по итоговому результату может скрывать невалидное поведение агента. BizBench предлагается как инструмент для развития надёжных агентов, соблюдающих ограничения, а не только завершающих задачу.

en.title: Evaluating Agents Beyond Success: The BizBench Approach
en.desc: BizBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate long-horizon business agents by focusing on their ability to maintain execution validity during complex tasks. Unlike traditional benchmarks that only measure final success, BizBench assesses how well agents adhere to real-world constraints throughout their operations. It incorporates a variety of tasks that reflect the challenges faced in business environments, such as conflicting policies and resource limitations. The findings highlight that even advanced models struggle with maintaining compliance, indicating the need for improved evaluation methods in machine learning applications.

zh.title: BizBench：超越任务完成的长时间代理评估
zh.desc: BizBench 是一个评估长时间业务代理的基准，关注中间执行的有效性。尽管一些先进模型在最终目标上取得了一定成功，但它们常常违反执行过程中的约束。该基准通过真实的支付程序，整合了大量知识文档和业务工具，提供了一个可执行的环境。实验结果显示，许多模型在执行有效性方面存在显著不足，强调了在复杂商业环境中可靠执行的重要性。

papers.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
papers.abstract: Abstract ACT3D trains vision-language models via reinforcement learning to actively explore 3D environments from single first-person views, improving answer accuracy through adaptive, question-conditioned navigation without direct exploration supervision.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only as an environment with which the model can interact through actions (e.g., move left) and observations (rendered images). Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question. The model can then iteratively reason, navigate, and reorient its viewpoint before committing to a final answer. Following an initial trajectory-supervised finetuning, we apply reinforcement learning (RL) with rewards driven primarily by final-answer correctness. Crucially, RL provides no direct supervision over which viewpoints the model should visit or which exploration actions it should take. Instead, the model must learn an effective exploration policy solely from the extent to which its interactions improve performance. Across six 3D benchmarks, our model ACT3D achieves an average accuracy of 53.2% that improves its base Qwen model by 22.0% and surpasses proprietary Gemini 3.6 Flash. ACT3D also outperforms existing open-source 3D methods while using 50-70% fewer input frames, and generalizes to unseen domains with an average improvement of 5.9% over its supervised initialization. Further analysis reveals adaptive, question-conditioned exploration. Performance gains over the base model increase from 0.6% on questions answerable from the initial view to 16.3% on those requiring extensive exploration. ACT3D searches for occluded targets, avoids unnecessary exploration, and acquires complementary viewpoints for spatial comparisons. These findings demonstrate that outcome-based RL enables VLMs not only to reason over visual evidence, but also to learn when and how to acquire it.

ru.title: Учимся не только смотреть, но и выбирать, куда смотреть в 3D
ru.desc: В статье представлен ACT3D — визуально-языковая модель (VLM), которая учится активно исследовать 3D-пространство, получая на вход лишь одно изображение от первого лица, как это делают люди. Модель сначала проходит supervised finetuning на траекториях, а затем обучается с помощью reinforcement learning, где награда зависит только от правильности финального ответа, без прямой разметки того, какие ракурсы посещать. Модель выполняет действия навигации (например, движение влево) и получает отрендеренные наблюдения, что позволяет ей адаптивно менять точку обзора под конкретный вопрос. На шести 3D-бенчмарках ACT3D показывает в среднем 53.2% точности, улучшая базовую Qwen-модель на 22% и используя на 50-70% меньше входных кадров, чем существующие методы.

en.title: Exploring 3D Worlds: Learning to Navigate with Vision-Language Models
en.desc: The paper presents ACT3D, a method for training vision-language models (VLMs) to explore 3D environments using reinforcement learning (RL). Instead of relying on multiple views or 3D models, ACT3D uses a single first-person image and allows the model to navigate and interact with the environment to answer questions. The model learns to explore effectively by receiving rewards based on the correctness of its final answers, without direct supervision on which actions to take. Results show that ACT3D significantly improves accuracy and generalizes well to new environments, demonstrating the power of RL in enhancing VLMs' exploration capabilities.

zh.title: 主动探索3D环境的视觉-语言模型
zh.desc: ACT3D通过强化学习训练视觉-语言模型，使其能够从单一的第一人称视角主动探索3D环境。模型在没有直接探索监督的情况下，通过适应性的问题条件导航来提高答案的准确性。与传统方法不同，ACT3D仅使用单张图像进行学习，模拟人类的视觉处理方式。实验结果表明，ACT3D在多个3D基准测试中表现优异，显著提高了模型的性能。

papers.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract HexaShell is a coding agent that controls a dual-arm robot via vision and self-written tools, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo but struggling with contact-heavy tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now compete with learned policies on robot manipulation leaderboards. We ask how far a coding agent can go when it controls a robot instead of a computer, and where it stops. Our system, HexaShell, keeps the harness thin: it only turns the agent's commands into robot motion. The agent drives a robot with two arms through one command line. It sees three RGB cameras and knows their calibration. After each failed attempt, the agent reads the log, finds the cause, and writes or fixes small programs called tools. In this way it keeps what it learns as code, as a coding agent does when it fixes a failing test. The tools may use only what the robot observes. They use triangulation to find where objects are, relative to each other and to the gripper. If two cameras see the same point, the point lies where the two camera rays meet. If a point lies on a known plane, such as the table or the top of a block, it lies where its ray meets that plane. When the head camera is not enough, the robot moves a wrist camera to get a second view. We build the tools on only ten layouts of one seed per task, then freeze them and test them on ten new layouts of the same seed. We use Codex with GPT-6-Astra at medium reasoning effort. On all 42 RoboDojo tasks, HexaShell reaches a success rate of 39.7% and a progress score of 48.0, averaged in the same way as the leaderboard. This is a new state of the art on RoboDojo. The limit is contact, not reasoning: pushing reaches 92.5% and memory tasks 65.0%, but tight insertion only 8.3%. When the agent fails, it usually sees the failure but cannot make the motion work. We open source the tools evolved so far at https://github.com/HexaFuture/HexaShell.

ru.title: Агент-программист научился управлять роботом, но контакт остаётся его слабым местом
ru.desc: В статье представлен HexaShell — coding agent на базе vision language model (VLM), который управляет двурукой роботизированной платформой через командную строку и три RGB-камеры. Агент после каждой неудачной попытки анализирует лог, находит причину и пишет или исправляет небольшие программы-инструменты, которые сохраняют накопленный опыт в виде кода. Инструменты используют триангуляцию и пересечение лучей с известной плоскостью, а на 42 задачах RoboDojo система достигает нового state of the art с success rate 39.7%. Главное ограничение — не рассуждения, а контакт: задачи толкания решаются почти идеально, а сложная вставка — лишь в 8.3% случаев.

en.title: HexaShell: A Coding Agent for Robotic Mastery
en.desc: HexaShell is an innovative coding agent designed to control a dual-arm robot using visual inputs and self-generated tools. It achieves impressive results on the RoboDojo platform, although it faces challenges with tasks that require physical contact. The agent utilizes vision language models to interpret commands and translate them into robotic movements, while also learning from failures by creating and refining small programs called tools. The research highlights the agent's strengths in reasoning and observation, but also identifies limitations in executing contact-heavy tasks, paving the way for future improvements in robotic manipulation.

zh.title: 编码代理驱动双臂机器人，开创机器人操作新纪元
zh.desc: HexaShell 是一个编码代理，通过视觉和自编工具控制双臂机器人，在 RoboDojo 上取得了最先进的成果，但在接触密集的任务中表现不佳。该系统利用视觉语言模型（VLMs）生成，能够与学习的策略在机器人操作排行榜上竞争。HexaShell 通过一条命令行驱动机器人，利用三台 RGB 摄像头进行观察，并在每次失败后分析日志，找出原因并编写或修复小程序。该系统在 42 个 RoboDojo 任务中取得了 39.7% 的成功率，显示出其在推理方面的潜力，但在紧密插入任务中表现有限。

papers.title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
papers.abstract: Abstract Researchers benchmarked AI agents on open scientific problems by having them draft follow-up papers from unpublished directions, finding that none met expert standards and most contained fabricated claims or contradictory evidence.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Can AI agents carry out research on open scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, a benchmark that provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write a follow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of a follow-up paper is challenging in general, using these conditions to form a rubric makes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer. We have nine frontier agents write 15 follow-ups each, spanning quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning domains. None of the 135 submissions satisfies all the conditions, and 114 fail our integrity check, most often because the paper claims work that was never done or reports numbers that contradict the recorded evidence. Overall, agents readily produce papers that look like follow-ups, but none meets the standard of the domain scientist, leaving substantial headroom. Our code and data are publicly available.
affiliations: Ss.Cyril and Methodius University of Skopje

ru.title: AI-агенты пишут статьи как учёные, но пока без настоящей науки
ru.desc: Автор статьи создал бенчмарк Into the Unknown, в котором AI-агенты получают научную статью и исследовательское направление и должны написать продолжение. Направления предложили учёные национальных лабораторий DOE, а оценка проводилась по rubric, основанной на их требованиях к работе. Из 135 сгенерированных работ ни одна не выполнила все условия, а 114 не прошли проверку честности, чаще всего из-за выдуманных результатов или противоречий с данными. Вывод: агенты умеют имитировать научные статьи, но до уровня экспертов в области им ещё далеко.

en.title: AI Agents Struggle to Meet Scientific Standards in Research
en.desc: This paper evaluates the ability of AI agents to conduct research by generating follow-up papers on open scientific problems. The study introduces a benchmark called 'Into the Unknown', where agents are given a scientific paper and a research direction to create a new paper. Despite producing numerous submissions across various scientific fields, none of the AI-generated papers met the expert standards set by domain scientists, with many containing false claims or contradictory data. The findings highlight the current limitations of AI in producing credible scientific research, indicating significant room for improvement.

zh.title: AI代理在科学研究中的挑战与机遇
zh.desc: 本研究评估了人工智能代理在开放科学问题上的表现，要求它们撰写未发表方向的后续论文。结果显示，所有生成的论文都未达到专家标准，大多数包含虚假声明或矛盾证据。研究团队与美国能源部国家实验室的科学家合作，制定了评估标准，以便更好地评估这些后续论文的质量。尽管代理能够生成看似合理的论文，但没有一篇符合领域科学家的要求，表明在这一领域仍有很大的改进空间。

papers.title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets
papers.abstract: Abstract LiveMACEBench evaluates persistent LLM agents in live financial markets using decision traces to reveal gaps between outcomes and underlying capabilities.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Evaluating agents by outcomes alone can obscure the capabilities that produce them. This problem is especially pronounced in evolving environments, where outcomes reflect a closed-loop interaction between agent behavior and changing external conditions. We introduce LiveMACEBench, a process-aware benchmark that uses live financial markets as a naturally evolving testbed for persistent LLM agents. Five frontier LLMs operate along continuous trajectories under matched Tool Use, Persistent Memory, Rule Following, and Multi-Agent Collaboration configurations. We evaluate them through both realized outcomes and mechanism-specific diagnostics derived from complete decision traces. Across 30 days of live evaluation, we find a pronounced outcome-capability gap: realized returns often diverge from capability-specific measurements, and similar outcomes can arise from markedly different patterns of mechanism use. Trace-level diagnostics further expose distinct bottlenecks across capabilities, demonstrating that mechanism access, effective mechanism use, and downstream performance are not interchangeable measures of agent capability. LiveMACEBench makes this distinction measurable, turning live markets from a performance leaderboard into a diagnostic environment for agent capability

ru.title: Не только доходность: оцениваем способности AI-агентов по процессу, а не по результату
ru.desc: Статья представляет LiveMACEBench — новый бенчмарк для оценки persistent LLM-агентов в реальных финансовых рынках. Авторы показывают, что оценка только по итоговой доходности скрывает реальные способности агента, поскольку схожий результат может возникать при совершенно разных паттернах использования инструментов и памяти. Пять frontier LLM тестировались 30 дней в условиях Tool Use, Persistent Memory, Rule Following и Multi-Agent Collaboration, с анализом полных decision traces. Работа доказывает, что доступ к механизмам, их эффективное использование и итоговая производительность — разные метрики, и что live-рынки можно превратить из таблицы лидеров в диагностическую среду для оценки возможностей агентов.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: Evaluating LLM Agents Beyond Outcomes
en.desc: LiveMACEBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate persistent large language model (LLM) agents in real-time financial markets. It focuses on understanding the differences between the outcomes achieved by these agents and the underlying capabilities that lead to those outcomes. By analyzing decision traces, the benchmark reveals that similar results can stem from different mechanisms, highlighting the importance of capability-specific diagnostics. This approach allows for a deeper understanding of agent performance in dynamic environments, making it possible to identify specific strengths and weaknesses in their decision-making processes.

zh.title: 揭示能力与结果之间的差距
zh.desc: LiveMACEBench 是一个评估持久性大型语言模型（LLM）代理在实时金融市场表现的基准工具。它通过决策轨迹揭示结果与基础能力之间的差距，尤其是在不断变化的环境中，这种差距更加明显。该基准允许在匹配的工具使用、持久记忆、规则遵循和多代理协作配置下，评估五种前沿 LLM 的表现。通过对30天的实时评估，我们发现实际收益与能力特定测量之间存在显著差距，表明代理能力的评估需要更全面的诊断。

papers.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract CarryOn organizes long-horizon agent context around reusable task objects rather than interaction histories, improving efficiency and performance on complex benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-horizon agents accumulate progress in persistent task state, yet repeatedly process interaction histories describing how that progress was achieved. This raises a natural question: can long-horizon context instead be organized around reusable progress rather than the history that produced it? In this paper, we introduce CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes continuation around reusable task objects. Rather than treating compressed histories or reconstructed accounts of progress as the primary basis for continuation, CarryOn builds a context view from continuation carriers, complementary execution context, and a live tail of recent interactions. A core challenge is keeping this reusable basis valid after its surrounding history is retired: how can CarryOn update the basis without reconstructing the full representation at every fold? CarryOn maintains carrier records across folds, revising affected records against bound evidence and applicable environment checks while carrying forward unaffected records and jointly updating execution context. Experiments on OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus show improved gains of 5.8% and 7.0% while reducing total token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%, respectively. Project page: https://ethannju.github.io/carryon

ru.title: Помнить прогресс, а не историю: переиспользуемый контекст для LLM-агентов
ru.desc: В статье представлен CarryOn — объектно-ориентированный контекстный рантайм для LLM-агентов, работающих над длинными задачами. Вместо хранения и повторной обработки истории взаимодействий система строит контекст из переиспользуемых task-объектов (continuation carriers), дополнительного контекста выполнения и последних шагов. При сворачивании истории записи carriers обновляются по связанным доказательствам и проверкам окружения, а неизменённые записи переносятся без пересборки. На бенчмарках OSWorld 2.0 и BrowseComp-Plus метод даёт прирост качества на 5.8% и 7.0% и снижает расход токенов на 51.9% и 22.9%.

en.title: Revolutionizing Long-Horizon Context with Reusable Task Objects
en.desc: The paper introduces CarryOn, a novel approach for organizing long-horizon agent context using reusable task objects instead of traditional interaction histories. This method enhances efficiency and performance in complex benchmarks by focusing on the progress made rather than the detailed history of actions taken. CarryOn employs an object-oriented context runtime that maintains a live tail of recent interactions while updating reusable task objects without needing to reconstruct full histories. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in performance metrics and reductions in token usage, showcasing the effectiveness of this new framework.

zh.title: CarryOn：重用任务对象提升长时间代理效率
zh.desc: CarryOn 是一种新的方法，它通过可重用的任务对象来组织长时间的代理上下文，而不是依赖于交互历史。这种方法提高了在复杂基准测试中的效率和性能。CarryOn 通过维护载体记录和更新执行上下文，避免了每次都重建完整表示的问题。实验结果显示，CarryOn 在 OSWorld 2.0 和 BrowseComp-Plus 上分别提高了 5.8% 和 7.0% 的性能，同时减少了总令牌使用量。

papers.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract Speculative Sampling enables interactive video generation with large bidirectional windows by caching predictions and delivering them incrementally, reducing latency without sacrificing quality.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted future remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk sampling. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and sampling time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Большие окна для качества видео без потери скорости
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают метод Speculative Sampling для интерактивной генерации видео, который позволяет использовать большие двунаправленные окна без роста задержки. Идея в том, что модель дополняет окно шумовыми latent-векторами как padding, а предсказания кэшируются и выдаются инкрементально, при этом непоздно зафиксированное будущее можно заменить. Анализ задержки показывает, что это снимает нижнюю границу ожидания, связанную с границами чанков, и смещает оптимизацию на ускорение сэмплирования каждого чанка. Размер двунаправленного окна становится параметром, который balance-ит качество видео и время сэмплирования, без сложного streaming post-training.

en.title: Enhancing Interactive Video with Speculative Sampling
en.desc: The paper introduces Speculative Sampling, a method for improving interactive video generation by using larger bidirectional windows while maintaining low latency. By caching predictions and allowing for incremental delivery, it enhances video quality and leverages GPU parallelism effectively. The approach involves appending noise latents as padding to expand the modeling window, which allows for better reuse of predictions. This strategy shifts the focus from merely reducing chunk sizes to optimizing both visual quality and sampling time, enabling more efficient interactive streaming of large models.

zh.title: 推测采样：提升交互式视频生成的质量与效率
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种名为“推测采样”的新策略，用于交互式视频生成。该方法通过缓存预测结果并逐步传递，减少了延迟，同时保持了视频质量。研究表明，使用较大的双向窗口可以更好地利用GPU并行性，从而提高视频生成的质量。推测采样允许在不牺牲低延迟交互的情况下，优化视觉质量和采样时间。

papers.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality. However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes. In this work, we introduce Scene-Designer, an agentic framework that learns design intelligence through complementary design and critique experiences. We construct two datasets: Scene-OTA-35K, which provides Observation--Thought--Action supervision for learning scene design and efficient error correction, and Scene-OTC-15K, which provides Observation--Thought--Critic supervision for learning scene quality critique across physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence. Based on these experiences, we propose Scene-GRPO, a Critic-guided GRPO framework that improves design decisions and reduces unnecessary trial-and-error corrections. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Scene-Designer achieves superior performance in physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence, while the learned Scene-Critic significantly outperforms general-purpose models in scene critique. Moreover, test-time Critic guidance further improves scene generation, showing that the Critic can provide useful guidance beyond training. Additional analysis suggests a trend of mutual enhancement between scene design and critique abilities.

ru.title: Агент, который учится и проектировать, и критиковать 3D-интерьеры
ru.desc: Статья представляет Scene-Designer — агентную систему на базе LLM, которая генерирует связные и физически корректные 3D-сцены интерьера по текстовому описанию. Авторы создали два датасета: Scene-OTA-35K для обучения проектированию и исправлению ошибок, и Scene-OTC-15K для обучения Critic-модели, оценивающей качество сцены. Метод Scene-GRPO использует Critic для направления обучения с подкреплением (GRPO), что снижает количество лишних итераций исправления. Эксперименты показывают превосходство над универсальными моделями как в генерации, так и в критике, а также взаимное усиление способностей проектирования и оценки.

en.title: Enhancing 3D Scene Generation through Design and Critique Integration
en.desc: This paper presents Scene-Designer, a framework that enhances the generation of 3D indoor scenes from natural language by integrating design and critique processes. It introduces two datasets, Scene-OTA-35K and Scene-OTC-15K, which help the model learn how to design scenes and evaluate their quality effectively. The proposed Scene-GRPO framework utilizes a Critic to guide design decisions, minimizing errors and improving the overall quality of generated scenes. Experimental results show that Scene-Designer excels in aspects like physical validity and layout coherence, demonstrating the benefits of combining design intelligence with critique capabilities.

zh.title: 设计与批评的智能提升3D场景生成
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种名为Scene-Designer的框架，旨在通过设计和批评的互补经验来学习设计智能，从而生成完整、一致且可用的3D室内场景。我们构建了两个数据集，分别用于学习场景设计和场景质量批评，涵盖物理有效性、功能正确性和布局一致性。基于这些经验，我们提出了Critic-guided GRPO框架，能够改善设计决策并减少不必要的试错过程。实验结果表明，Scene-Designer在多个评估指标上表现优越，且批评者在测试阶段的指导进一步提升了场景生成的质量。

papers.title: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
papers.abstract: Abstract OpenMobile-2 is an open mobile agent trained with diverse simulated apps, large-scale supervised and reinforcement learning data, and hybrid GUI-tool use, achieving strong benchmark results and real-device transfer.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce OpenMobile-2, a near-frontier mobile agent with fully open training environments and recipes. We make three key advances: (1) Diverse environments with simulated commercial apps: We build MobileGym++, featuring 35 realistic, functionally rich commercial-style apps with cross-app workflows, while preserving full controllability for reset and verification. Together with newly configured apps in Android emulators, this yields a diverse playground spanning over 110 apps. (2) Open training data at scale: Building on this foundation, we curate nearly 12K mobile interaction trajectories for supervised fine-tuning and the largest open collection of verifiable RL training data for mobile agents, comprising over 2K executable tasks with automatic rewards. (3) Hybrid GUI and app-native tool use: We explore an experimental mobile-use setting where apps expose selected functionalities as app-native tools alongside their GUIs, allowing agents to interleave GUI actions and tool calls within a task. We implement this setting in MobileGym++ with over 300 carefully scoped tools across 50+ apps. Additionally, we introduce MobileGym++ Bench for complex, long-horizon commercial mobile scenarios, supporting both GUI-only and hybrid GUI-tool evaluation on a shared task suite. OpenMobile-2 performs competitively across established benchmarks, including AndroidWorld (79.9) and MobileWorld (50.4), while showing promising transfer to real-device mobile use, nearly doubling SPA-Bench performance from 31.9 to 59.6. All resources are available at https://os-copilot.github.io/OpenMobile2-Home/.

ru.title: Открытый мобильный агент, который управляет телефоном через GUI и инструменты
ru.desc: Статья представляет OpenMobile-2, открытого мобильного AI-агента, обученного в полностью открытых средах и на открытых данных. Авторы создали MobileGym++ с 35 функционально богатыми приложениями и собрали около 12 тысяч траекторий для supervised fine-tuning и крупнейший открытый набор верифицируемых данных для RL с автоматическими наградами. Агент использует гибридный режим, сочетая действия через GUI с вызовами app-native инструментов, которых более 300. Модель показывает конкурентные результаты на бенчмарках AndroidWorld и MobileWorld и хорошо переносится на реальные устройства.

en.title: Empowering Mobile Agents with Open Training and Diverse Environments
en.desc: OpenMobile-2 is a mobile agent designed to operate in diverse simulated environments, specifically tailored with commercial-style apps. It utilizes a combination of supervised and reinforcement learning techniques, leveraging a large dataset of mobile interaction trajectories for effective training. The agent can seamlessly integrate GUI actions with app-native tools, enhancing its ability to perform complex tasks. OpenMobile-2 demonstrates strong performance on benchmark tests and shows significant potential for real-world application, indicating its robustness and adaptability.

zh.title: 开放移动智能体的未来
zh.desc: OpenMobile-2 是一个开放的移动智能体，经过多样化的模拟应用程序训练，结合了大规模的监督学习和强化学习数据，取得了强大的基准结果和真实设备的迁移能力。我们构建了 MobileGym++，提供了 35 个功能丰富的商业风格应用程序，形成了一个多样化的训练环境。我们还整理了近 12,000 条移动交互轨迹用于监督微调，并创建了最大的可验证强化学习训练数据集。通过混合使用图形用户界面和应用原生工具，OpenMobile-2 能够在任务中交替执行 GUI 操作和工具调用，展现出优异的性能。

papers.title: BridgeWAM: Bridging Video and Action Experts via Latent Bridge Queries
papers.abstract: Abstract BridgeWAM decouples video and action experts via latent bridge queries to improve action prediction efficiency and generalization in world action models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small World Action Models (WAMs) commonly couple video and action experts through dense, layer-wise Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention, exposing action prediction to irrelevant visual features while enforcing matched expert depths. This coupling hinders selective visual-feature use and introduces redundant computation. We introduce Bridge-of-Experts (BoE), instantiated as BridgeWAM, which aggregates visual, language, and proprioceptive priors through 32 Latent Bridge Queries (LBQs) into a shared, limited latent space. Joint video-action supervision lets action gradients guide the Video Expert toward representations better suited for action prediction, while the Action Expert learns to selectively retrieve task-relevant information through cross-attention. Decoupling expert depths and reusing LBQs during action denoising yield a 5.06B model with a 30-layer Video Expert and a two-layer Action Expert, achieving 98.25% success on LIBERO and 72.24% pooled success on LIBERO-Plus, demonstrating effective task execution and strong generalization with an ultralight action head. Ablations support joint representation adaptation and unified LBQ conditioning. Relative to Fast-WAM, BridgeWAM reduces single-sample inference FLOPs by 28.72% in simulation profiling and real-robot latency to 77.1 ms (a 2.47-fold speedup). Qualitative experimental results further indicate preferential attention to target objects and task destinations across perturbations.
affiliations: Institute of automation, Chinese academy of science

ru.title: Мост между видением и действием: быстрее и точнее управляем роботов
ru.desc: В статье предложена архитектура BridgeWAM для World Action Models, где видео-эксперт и action-эксперт разделены через Latent Bridge Queries: 32 обучаемых запроса агрегируют визуальные, языковые и проприоцептивные признаки в общее компактное латентное пространство. Совместное обучение на видео и действиях позволяет градиентам от action-предсказания адаптировать представления видео-эксперта, а action-эксперт избирательно извлекает релевантную информацию через cross-attention. Развязка глубины экспертов дает модель на 5.06 млрд параметров с 30-слойным видео-экспертом и двухслойным action-экспертом, которая достигает 98.25% успеха на LIBERO и 72.24% на LIBERO-Plus. По сравнению с Fast-WAM вывод становится быстрее: FLOPs снижаются на 28.72%, а задержка на реальном роботе составляет 77.1 мс.

en.title: Decoupling Experts for Efficient Action Prediction
en.desc: The paper presents BridgeWAM, a novel approach that separates video and action experts using Latent Bridge Queries (LBQs) to enhance action prediction efficiency and generalization in world action models. Traditional methods couple these experts tightly, leading to inefficiencies and irrelevant visual feature processing. By decoupling the experts and allowing them to operate in a shared latent space, the model can focus on relevant information while reducing computational redundancy. The results show significant improvements in action prediction accuracy and speed, demonstrating the effectiveness of this new architecture in real-world applications.

zh.title: 解耦视频与动作专家，提高动作预测效率
zh.desc: BridgeWAM通过潜在桥查询将视频和动作专家解耦，以提高世界动作模型中的动作预测效率和泛化能力。传统的Mixture-of-Transformers注意力机制将视频和动作专家紧密结合，导致动作预测受到无关视觉特征的影响。BridgeWAM引入了专家桥接（BoE），通过32个潜在桥查询将视觉、语言和本体感知先验聚合到一个共享的潜在空间中。该方法在LIBERO和LIBERO-Plus数据集上取得了显著的成功率，展示了其在任务执行和泛化能力上的有效性。

papers.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
papers.abstract: Abstract AI agents evaluated on physics research tasks show strong local scientific results but frequently fail to fully resolve research questions due to incomplete evidence and unresolved applicability limits.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Can AI agents organize scientific investigations that lead to well-supported conclusions? To evaluate this capability, we introduce PhysClosureBench, a benchmark of 50 expert-verified, goal-specified research tasks spanning strong-field, attosecond, and neighboring physics areas. Each task specifies the research objective and essential scientific constraints, while leaving the agent to organize the investigation and determine how to generate and validate the evidence needed to answer the question. A 20-criterion Atomic Score measures local scientific accomplishment, while Research Closure (RC0--RC4) assesses how fully the investigation resolves the specified research question based on whether its indispensable evidence requirements and applicable scope conditions are satisfied. We evaluate seven frontier LLMs, where Claude-Opus-5 achieves the highest mean Atomic Score (6.29/10) but reaches RC4 in only 32.7% of attempts. Across the benchmark, 36.2% of attempts scoring at least 8/10 still fall short of RC4, while all seven models reach RC4 on substantially fewer tasks in all three runs than in at least one. Case-level analysis further illustrates how misinterpretation of generated results and unresolved physical applicability limits can lead to incomplete closure. Together, these results reveal a persistent gap between AI agents' local scientific accomplishments and their ability to achieve complete research closure.
affiliations: The HongKong University of Science and Technology(Guangzhou)

ru.title: AI-агенты умеют находить результаты, но не доводят исследование до конца
ru.desc: Статья представляет PhysClosureBench — бенчмарк из 50 экспертно проверенных исследовательских задач по физике сильного поля, аттосекундной физике и смежным областям. Агенты на основе LLM оцениваются по 20-критериальной метрике Atomic Score и по шкале Research Closure (RC0–RC4), которая показывает, насколько полно выполнены обязательные требования к доказательствам и границы применимости. Лучшая модель Claude-Opus-5 получает высокий средний Atomic Score (6.29/10), но достигает RC4 лишь в 32.7% попыток. Авторы делают вывод о существенном разрыве между локальными научными результатами AI-агентов и их способностью полностью закрыть исследовательский вопрос.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: AI in Scientific Research Closure
en.desc: This paper introduces PhysClosureBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to conduct scientific investigations in physics. It presents 50 expert-verified tasks that require agents to organize research and generate evidence to answer specific questions. The study measures local scientific success using an Atomic Score and assesses the completeness of investigations through Research Closure criteria. Results show that while some AI models perform well locally, they often struggle to fully resolve research questions due to issues like misinterpretation of results and limitations in applicability.

zh.title: AI代理在科学研究中的挑战与机遇
zh.desc: 本论文探讨了人工智能代理在物理研究任务中的表现，尽管它们在局部科学成果上表现良好，但常常无法完全解决研究问题。我们引入了PhysClosureBench，这是一个包含50个专家验证的研究任务的基准，旨在评估AI代理组织科学调查的能力。每个任务都指定了研究目标和必要的科学约束，AI代理需要自行组织调查并生成和验证证据。研究结果显示，尽管一些大型语言模型在局部科学成就上得分较高，但在完全解决研究问题方面仍存在显著差距。

papers.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
papers.abstract: Abstract Lexical reference frames interpret hidden states through a model's own remaining layers, enabling accurate attribution, steering, and early layer exit.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does. We argue that every hidden state has a native reference frame, induced by the layers that read it next and adaptive to the context. Lexical reference frames approximate it by reading a state through the model's own remaining layers with a stated number of rounds of attention between positions and a typical attention output for the rest, without fitting to the model's output. No lens, with fixed directions per layer, can exceed the square root of the native frame's coherence, 0.30 and 0.35 at mid-depth of SmolLM3-3B and OLMo3-7B, whereas the first-order frame, LexFrame[1], reaches 0.97 and 0.97 and reads a state within 0.16 nats of the model's output. Its coefficients attribute predictions more faithfully than attribution patching, its lexical basis steers a prediction while sparing other tokens, and its confident readings would let an early exit skip 0.45 and 0.42 of the layers, where lenses skip almost none. In this way, lexical reference frames make every hidden state of the model readable, attributable and steerable.

ru.title: Каждое скрытое состояние LLM читается изнутри самой модели
ru.desc: Статья предлагает понятие «лексического опорного фрейма» (lexical reference frame), который интерпретирует скрытое состояние LLM через оставшиеся слои самой модели, а не через фиксированный lens. Метод LexFrame[1] почти точно воспроизводит выход модели (расхождение 0.16 nats) и превосходит существующие lens-методы по когерентности. На его основе можно точнее атрибутировать предсказания, управлять генерацией конкретных токенов и делать early exit, пропуская около 45% слоёв. Таким образом каждое скрытое состояние модели становится читаемым, объяснимым и управляемым.

en.title: Unlocking Hidden States with Lexical Reference Frames
en.desc: This paper introduces the concept of lexical reference frames, which help interpret hidden states in language models by utilizing the model's own layers. Unlike traditional methods that either use fixed lenses or treat states as point clouds, lexical reference frames adaptively read hidden states based on the context and the layers that follow. The authors demonstrate that these frames can achieve higher coherence and more accurate predictions compared to existing techniques, allowing for better attribution and steering of model outputs. Additionally, they show that this approach enables early layer exits, improving efficiency without sacrificing performance.

zh.title: 词汇参考框架：让隐藏状态可读、可归因、可引导
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出了词汇参考框架的概念，用于通过模型的剩余层来解释隐藏状态，从而实现准确的归因、引导和早期层退出。论文指出，语言模型的词汇是其固有语义，嵌入和解嵌固定了残差流两端状态的含义。现有方法要么使用固定的视角，要么将状态视为点云，无法像模型那样读取状态。词汇参考框架通过模型自身的剩余层读取状态，使得每个隐藏状态都可以被理解、归因和引导。

papers.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract TreeOPSD enables long-horizon reinforcement learning for language model agents without critics by using tree-structured self-distillation with bounded updates derived from terminal rewards.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. However, training agents over long-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn-level credit assignment sparse and high-variance, while sequential mini-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the behavior policy. Existing approaches obtain denser credit via learned critics, process reward models, or on-policy distillation, but they rely on a value network, step-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher that increase training complexity. Meanwhile, importance sampling and clipping mitigate policy drift, but they do not specify a finite target that stops sequential updates from overshooting. In this work, we introduce TreeOPSD, a critic-free, tree-aware posterior self-distillation framework for long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning. Treating each interaction turn as a tree node, TreeOPSD branches alternative continuations from shared prefixes and recursively backs up terminal rewards into implicit turn-level credit. It then maps each credit to a closed-form, bounded teacher distribution parameterized by the likelihood ratio relative to the frozen behavior policy. Minimizing the divergence between this teacher and the student policy recovers the policy-gradient direction as the tangent at the behavior policy while bounding updates toward a finite target across sequential mini-batches. Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.

ru.title: Дерево решений вместо критика: честная награда для долгих агентских задач
ru.desc: В статье предложен метод TreeOPSD для обучения языковых агентов с подкреплением на длинных горизонтах без critic-сети. Каждый шаг взаимодействия представляется узлом дерева, из общих префиксов ветвятся альтернативные продолжения, а терминальная награда рекурсивно распространяется назад, формируя неявный credit assignment на уровне ходов. На основе этого строится ограниченное замкнутое teacher-распределение, зависящее от likelihood ratio относительно замороженной behavior policy, и student-политика обучается минимизацией дивергенции до него. Такой подход сохраняет направление policy gradient, ограничивает дрейф при последовательных mini-batch обновлениях и даёт прирост качества, например +4.97 пункта средней точности над GRPO на Deep Research.

en.title: Empowering Language Models with Tree-Structured Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Learning
en.desc: TreeOPSD is a novel framework designed for long-horizon reinforcement learning in language models that operates without the need for critics. It utilizes a tree-structured self-distillation approach to effectively manage the sparse and high-variance nature of terminal rewards by treating each interaction as a tree node. This method allows for the recursive backing up of rewards, creating a more efficient credit assignment process. By minimizing the divergence between a teacher distribution and the student policy, TreeOPSD ensures stable updates and enhances the performance of agents on complex tasks.

zh.title: 无评论者的长时间跨度强化学习新方法
zh.desc: TreeOPSD是一种用于长时间跨度强化学习的框架，旨在解决传统方法中的一些挑战。它通过树结构的自蒸馏方法，利用终端奖励来生成更密集的信用分配，而不需要使用评论者。该方法将每个交互回合视为树节点，并通过共享前缀分支出替代的继续路径，从而递归地将终端奖励传递到隐式的回合级信用。实验结果表明，TreeOPSD在多个基准测试中提升了智能体的能力，尤其是在长时间跨度任务中表现优异。

papers.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Abstract Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a 4B multimodal model that predicts masks from internal visual representations to improve fine-grained region reasoning and referring comprehension.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer. To close this gap, we present Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4B MLLM built on Qwen3.5 that predicts masks from its own visual representations. Specifically, a lightweight decoder combines vision-encoder patch features with visual latents, the language model's mask-token states, so mask supervision reaches the shared backbone without an additional segmentation encoder. Because each latent decodes to a mask, the model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents and thus think with visual latents, while grounded reasoning traces supervise the regions it visits during chain-of-thought. As a result, across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits, Xiaomi-Lens-0 gains 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 in referring comprehension and achieves the highest segmentation cIoU among compared models. Moreover, it surpasses Qwen3.5 across all perception benchmarks. Homepage: https://seerray-lab.github.io/Xiaomi-Lens-0{this https URL}

ru.title: Думай глазами: маски как часть рассуждений мультимодальной модели
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Xiaomi-Lens-0 — мультимодальную LLM на 4 млрд параметров, построенную на базе Qwen3.5, которая лучше понимает мелкие области изображения. Ключевая идея: модель предсказывает маски сегментации из собственных визуальных представлений, и для этого используется лёгкий декодер, объединяющий патч-признаки vision encoder и скрытые состояния mask-токенов языковой модели. Благодаря этому supervision по маскам напрямую обучает общий backbone без отдельного segmentation encoder, а модель может чередовать рассуждения с региональными латентными представлениями. В результате на всех восьми сплитах RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ и RefCOCOg прирост составляет в среднем 5.6 пункта, а по перцептивным бенчмаркам модель превосходит Qwen3.5.

en.title: Enhancing Image Understanding with Visual Mask Predictions
en.desc: Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a multimodal model designed to enhance understanding of specific regions within images by predicting masks from its internal visual representations. Traditional large language models often struggle with detailed image comprehension because they rely solely on text, which does not indicate which parts of an image are relevant to an answer. This model addresses that issue by integrating visual features with language processing, allowing it to generate masks that highlight important areas in an image. As a result, Xiaomi-Lens-0 significantly improves performance in referring comprehension tasks and achieves superior segmentation accuracy compared to previous models.

zh.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0：提升细粒度推理的多模态模型
zh.desc: Xiaomi-Lens-0 是一个具有 40 亿参数的多模态模型，旨在通过内部视觉表示预测掩码，从而提高细粒度区域推理和指代理解能力。传统的文本监督方法无法明确指定哪些区域支持答案，因此模型在细粒度区域理解上存在困难。Xiaomi-Lens-0 通过结合视觉编码器的特征和语言模型的掩码状态，使用轻量级解码器来解决这一问题。实验结果表明，该模型在 RefCOCO、RefCOCO+ 和 RefCOCOg 数据集上平均提高了 5.6 分，并在所有感知基准测试中超越了 Qwen3.5。

papers.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
papers.abstract: Abstract RAP introduces a large-scale dataset and benchmark for generating conference posters from papers as a visual coding task, providing verified paper-poster-markup triplets and both retrieval-based and trained generation methods.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Making a conference poster is visual coding in miniature: an entire paper must be compressed onto a single page, which exercises summarization, visual design, and code implementation at once, using nothing beyond the paper itself. Yet benchmarks for this task in the context of visual coding remain scarce: existing resources are small and annotated only with layout boxes, so evaluation must fall back on VLM-as-judge or human checklists rather than objective render-and-compare, and the generation methods they support design layouts from scratch, leaving human-crafted posters unusable as either a retrievable design library or as verified supervision. We introduce RAP (Reconstruct A Poster), a dataset and benchmark for paper-to-poster generation as a visual coding task. RAP contains 25K+ verified paper-poster pairs from various machine learning conferences held between 2022 and 2026, annotated with a three-level content taxonomy, plus a held-out benchmark of 150 test papers each paired with its human poster. A fully automated derendering pipeline turns each poster into styled HTML/CSS of typed, refillable slots, so every sample is a paper-poster-markup triplet verifiable by rendering against the source poster. The corpus serves both inference and training: PosterRAG, a training-free multi-agent pipeline, retrieves an exemplar and refills its slots without touching layout or styling, while an SFT+RL recipe trains a dedicated model from the same triplets. An online demo is available at https://reconstruct-a-poster.github.io/.

ru.title: От статьи к постеру: генерация научных постеров как визуальный кодинг
ru.desc: Статья представляет RAP — большой датасет и бенчмарк для автоматической генерации научных постеров по статьям, рассматриваемой как задача визуального кодинга. Датасет содержит более 25 тысяч проверенных пар «статья–постер» с конференций по машинному обучению (2022–2026), а также тестовые примеры с человеческими постерами. Постеры автоматически переводятся в HTML/CSS с заполняемыми слотами, что позволяет верифицировать результат рендерингом. Предложены два подхода: PosterRAG, не требующий обучения, который извлекает похожий шаблон и заполняет его содержимым, и модель, обученную через SFT+RL на этих данных.

en.title: Transforming Papers into Posters: A Visual Coding Revolution
en.desc: The RAP paper introduces a new dataset and benchmark aimed at generating conference posters from academic papers, treating this as a visual coding challenge. It provides over 25,000 verified pairs of papers and their corresponding posters, annotated with a detailed content taxonomy. The dataset allows for both retrieval-based methods and trained generation techniques, enhancing the evaluation of poster generation through objective comparisons. This initiative addresses the lack of comprehensive resources in visual coding by offering a structured approach to poster creation, leveraging automated tools for rendering and verification.

zh.title: 重建海报：视觉编码的新标准
zh.desc: RAP（重建海报）是一个用于从论文生成会议海报的大规模数据集和基准，旨在将视觉编码任务进行标准化。该数据集包含超过25,000对经过验证的论文-海报配对，涵盖2022至2026年间的各种机器学习会议，并附有三层内容分类注释。RAP提供了基于检索和训练生成的方法，支持自动化的海报渲染和验证，确保生成的海报与原始论文一致。该研究为视觉编码任务提供了新的评估标准，推动了海报生成技术的发展。

papers.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
papers.abstract: Abstract MIST separates scene setup from change execution to isolate memory failures in video world models, and M3-Agent improves instruction execution to significantly boost benchmark scores.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.

ru.title: Сначала научите модель сделать движение — и только потом судите о её памяти
ru.desc: В статье предлагается MIST — новый метод оценки памяти video world model, который разделяет установку сцены и выполнение изменения, чтобы не путать провал памяти с невыполнением инструкции. Авторы показывают, что у модели часто правильно строится сцена, но не выполняется нужное изменение, и эта проблема проявляется и в общих тестах памяти. Для её решения предложен M3-Agent, который рекурсивно уточняет детали входной инструкции, без изменения замороженной модели. Метод более чем утраивает показатель MIST reveal и улучшает результаты на бенчмарках WRBench и MBench-T, устанавливая более строгий baseline.

en.title: Enhancing Memory Evaluation in Video Models with MIST and M3-Agent
en.desc: The paper introduces MIST, a method that evaluates memory in video world models by separating scene setup from the execution of changes. This approach allows for a clearer understanding of memory failures, as it distinguishes between setting a scene and actually carrying out changes. The authors also present M3-Agent, which enhances instruction execution by refining input commands to ensure that the model performs the requested actions. As a result, M3-Agent significantly improves benchmark scores, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing memory execution issues.

zh.title: 分离记忆与执行，提升模型表现
zh.desc: MIST是一种评估方法，它将场景设置与变更执行分开，以便更好地识别视频世界模型中的记忆失败。当前的测试将这些因素合并为一个分数，导致低分容易被误解为遗忘。M3-Agent通过递归修正输入指令的细节，显著提高了模型执行指令的能力，从而提升了基准测试的分数。该方法从执行的角度解决问题，展示了模型在明确指令后能够完成的操作，并设定了更严格的基准。

papers.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
papers.abstract: Abstract DLite improves speculative decoding for agentic AI by eliminating historical context maintenance and using target hidden states for local predictions, boosting acceptance length and reducing overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length, while maintaining their historical KV cache introduces substantial system overhead. In this paper, we identify the growing historical context as a common source of both problems and introduce DLite, a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI. DLite directly reuses contextual hidden states from the target model and performs local speculative prediction without explicitly maintaining the historical context, transforming an increasingly complex modeling problem into local simple prediction problem. A lightweight sequential head further restores intra-block causal dependencies with low overhead. To effectively train this heterogeneous history-free architecture, we introduce a tailored two-stage training strategy. Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2-6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.

ru.title: Ускоряем LLM-агентов, отказавшись от памяти контекста
ru.desc: Статья представляет DLite — фреймворк для speculative decoding в agentic AI, который не поддерживает историческое KV-кэширование, а использует скрытые состояния target-модели для локальных предсказаний. Авторы показывают, что существующие draft-модели теряют до 80% acceptance length на длинных многоходовых контекстах, а поддержка истории создаёт значительные системные издержки. Легковесная sequential head восстанавливает причинные зависимости внутри блока при низких накладных расходах, а двухэтапная стратегия обучения позволяет эффективно тренировать такую гетерогенную архитектуру. В экспериментах DLite достигает acceptance length 2–6 и превосходит state-of-the-art метод DSpark до 70%.

en.title: DLite: Simplifying Speculative Decoding for Better AI Performance
en.desc: DLite is a new framework designed to enhance speculative decoding for agentic AI by removing the need to maintain historical context. Instead of relying on past information, it uses hidden states from the target model to make predictions, which simplifies the process and reduces system overhead. This approach allows for better performance in long and evolving contexts, significantly increasing acceptance length. The paper also introduces a specialized two-stage training method to optimize this innovative architecture, demonstrating substantial improvements over existing methods.

zh.title: DLite：简化推测解码，提升代理AI性能
zh.desc: DLite是一种改进的推测解码框架，旨在提升代理AI的性能。它通过消除历史上下文的维护，直接利用目标模型的隐藏状态进行局部预测，从而提高接受长度并减少系统开销。传统的推测解码方法在处理复杂的上下文时表现不佳，而DLite通过简化建模问题，使得预测过程更加高效。实验结果表明，DLite在多种工作负载下的表现优于现有的推测解码方法，接受长度提升显著。

papers.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
papers.abstract: Abstract OfficeTown is a generative simulation framework that creates persistent professional organizations to generate work-grounded training data and evaluation benchmarks for AI agents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.

ru.title: Виртуальные офисы для обучения AI-агентов профессиональной работе
ru.desc: Статья представляет OfficeTown — фреймворк генеративной симуляции, который создаёт постоянно существующие профессиональные организации с сотрудниками, артефактами и решениями. На основе этих симуляций авторы формируют обучающие данные и бенчмарк OfficeTown Bench из 406 задач и 4836 критериев оценки для AI-агентов. Дообучение (SFT и on-policy distillation) на этих данных заметно улучшает модель Qwen3.5-9B на внешних бенчмарках, включая GDPval. Результаты показывают ценность организационной симуляции для создания реалистичных данных и сред для обучения универсальных агентов.

en.title: Empowering AI with Realistic Work Simulations
en.desc: OfficeTown is a simulation framework designed to create realistic professional organizations that generate training data for AI agents. It allows AI to learn from ongoing tasks and feedback within a simulated work environment, enhancing their ability to produce professional deliverables. The framework includes a variety of tasks and evaluation criteria, which help in assessing the performance of AI agents in real-world scenarios. By using OfficeTown, researchers can improve AI models through supervised fine-tuning, demonstrating the importance of organizational context in AI training.

zh.title: OfficeTown：生成工作基础数据的模拟框架
zh.desc: OfficeTown是一个生成性模拟框架，旨在创建持久的专业组织，以生成与工作相关的训练数据和评估基准。该框架通过自然语言描述组织的目的和活动，初始化一个成员协调工作的组织，并将任务分配给助手代理。OfficeTown生成的任务和上下文来自持续的组织工作，确保了决策和反馈的积累。研究表明，使用OfficeTown数据进行监督微调和策略蒸馏，可以显著提高AI代理在专业工作基准上的表现。

papers.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
papers.abstract: Abstract MOSS-Image is an open diffusion transformer that combines high-fidelity synthesis with intent-aware prompt enhancement to generate text-rich, layout-coherent images, achieving state-of-the-art open-weight results on long-form text and layout benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent closed-source image generation systems can produce diverse visual content from simple compositions to information-dense graphics, yet open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts. To narrow this gap, we introduce MOSS-Image, an open generation system that combines high-fidelity visual synthesis with intent-aware composition. First, we pretrain a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer (DiT) from scratch with a carefully designed recipe, enabling bilingual long-form text rendering and precise layout control. Second, we develop an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancement (PE) module that translates diverse user requests into detailed content and layout specifications. Together, they enable MOSS-Image to generate text-rich and layout-coherent images. We further introduce LongLongTextBench (LLTB) for evaluating long-form English and Chinese text rendering, and RealLayoutArena (RLA) for end-to-end layout-rich generation. MOSS-Image achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-weight models on LLTB, with an average text coverage of 96.3%. On RLA, MOSS-Image ranks second in the end-to-end system comparison, while its backbone ranks first among generators evaluated with shared enhanced prompts. We will release the model, training recipe, and evaluation framework to support further research and promote the text-to-image community.

ru.title: Открытая генерация изображений с точным текстом и макетом
ru.desc: Авторы представляют MOSS-Image — открытую диффузионную трансформер-модель (DiT) с 5 миллиардами параметров, обученную с нуля для генерации изображений. Модель использует агентный модуль улучшения промптов (prompt enhancement), который переводит запросы пользователя в детальные спецификации контента и layout. Такая связка позволяет качественно рендерить длинный двуязычный текст на английском и китайском и точно контролировать расположение элементов. На новых бенчмарках LongLongTextBench и RealLayoutArena модель показывает лучшие результаты среди открытых моделей.

en.title: MOSS-Image: Bridging Text and Visuals with Precision
en.desc: MOSS-Image is an innovative open diffusion transformer designed to generate high-quality images that effectively incorporate detailed text and complex layouts. It addresses the limitations of existing open-weight text-to-image models by utilizing a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer for enhanced bilingual text rendering and layout precision. The system features an intention-aware prompt enhancement module that translates user requests into specific content and layout instructions, resulting in coherent and informative images. MOSS-Image sets new benchmarks in long-form text rendering and layout generation, demonstrating superior performance in open-weight model evaluations.

zh.title: MOSS-Image：生成文本丰富的布局一致图像的创新模型
zh.desc: MOSS-Image是一种开放的扩散变换器，结合了高保真合成和意图感知的提示增强，能够生成文本丰富且布局一致的图像。该模型通过预训练一个5B单流扩散变换器，实现了双语长文本渲染和精确的布局控制。MOSS-Image还开发了一个意图感知的提示增强模块，将用户的多样请求转化为详细的内容和布局规范。通过这些创新，MOSS-Image在长文本和布局基准测试中取得了最先进的开放权重结果。

papers.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
papers.abstract: Abstract Visual image-generation training can expand pretrained multimodal models' knowledge, with alignment techniques improving text-based access to that visually acquired information.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Unified multimodal models (UMMs) receive image-generation supervision that exposes them to visual information not fully documented in text. Can learning to generate images expand what pretrained models know? We introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), a controlled protocol that supplies new knowledge through image-generation training and tests its accessibility through text-only question answering. Across seven knowledge categories and three UMMs, we observe direct but uneven transfer from visual supervision to language. Motivated by these observations, we successively introduce Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image--Text Alignment, which connect generation and answering through shared knowledge and interleaved responses, respectively. Guidance on selected entities can improve knowledge access on other entities without QA supervision, with additional gains from interleaved alignment. Further analysis shows that knowledge correctly reproduced in images is often more accessible through text, although substantial gaps remain between the two forms of access. These findings support visual generation as a source of knowledge beyond textual supervision, and motivate joint investigation of training data design and model architecture to make this knowledge more broadly accessible.

ru.title: Картинки учат модели тому, что не написано в тексте
ru.desc: Авторы исследуют, может ли обучение генерации изображений расширить знания предобученных унифицированных мультимодальных моделей (UMM). Они предлагают протокол Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), который передаёт новые знания через обучение генерации картинок, а затем проверяет их доступность через текстовые вопросы-ответы. Показано, что перенос знаний от визуального обучения к языку есть, но он неравномерный, поэтому авторы добавляют Textual Alignment и Interleaved Image-Text Alignment для связи генерации и ответов. Результаты подтверждают, что визуальная генерация может быть источником знаний помимо текстовых данных, однако между визуальной и текстовой формами доступа к знаниям сохраняются заметные разрывы.

en.title: Unlocking Knowledge: Bridging Visual Generation and Text Understanding
en.desc: This paper explores how training models to generate images can enhance their understanding of information that is not fully captured in text. It introduces a method called Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP) to evaluate how well new visual knowledge can be accessed through text-based questions. The authors find that while there is a direct transfer of knowledge from visual training to language tasks, the effectiveness varies across different knowledge categories. They propose techniques like Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image-Text Alignment to improve the connection between image generation and text comprehension, ultimately showing that visual knowledge can enrich language models.

zh.title: 视觉生成：超越文本监督的知识源
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了视觉图像生成训练如何扩展预训练的多模态模型的知识。通过对图像生成的监督，这些模型能够接触到文本中未充分记录的视觉信息。研究提出了知识转移探测（KTP）协议，旨在通过图像生成训练提供新知识，并测试其在文本问答中的可访问性。结果表明，视觉监督对语言知识的转移是直接但不均匀的，提示我们需要进一步研究训练数据设计和模型架构，以提高知识的可访问性。

papers.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
papers.abstract: Abstract DiscoveryRSI uses multi-agent evolutionary search and recursive learning to generate testable scientific hypotheses, improving quality through self-improvement and outperforming baseline agents on life-science benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Самообучающийся ИИ, который сам придумывает проверяемые научные гипотезы
ru.desc: В статье представлен фреймворк DiscoveryRSI, который использует мультиагентный эволюционный поиск и рекурсивное обучение (recursive learning) для генерации проверяемых научных гипотез. Авторы вводят операционное определение ценной гипотезы: обоснованное доказательствами утверждение, сопровождаемое выполнимым исследованием, явными критериями решения и альтернативными объяснениями. Система самосовершенствуется через оптимизацию кредитного назначения гипотез (hypothesis credit optimization), повтор harness-процессов и повторное открытие улучшений на новых задачах, а качество оценивается новым бенчмарком DFM-Bench. По результатам экспериментов в четырёх областях наук о жизни качество гипотез растёт с 4.86 до 5.39, а модель DiscoveryRSI-27B опережает базовые LLM-агенты по оценкам экспертов и по доле гипотез, совпавших с более поздними публикациями.

en.title: Revolutionizing Scientific Hypothesis Generation with DiscoveryRSI
en.desc: The paper presents DiscoveryRSI, a framework that enhances the generation of scientific hypotheses using multi-agent evolutionary search and recursive learning. It defines valuable hypotheses as evidence-based claims that address significant uncertainties and can be practically investigated. The framework employs mechanisms like hypothesis credit optimization and harness replay to improve research workflows and learning from past experiences. Evaluation results show that DiscoveryRSI significantly improves hypothesis quality and relevance in life-science domains compared to baseline models.

zh.title: 利用进化搜索提升科学假设质量
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为DiscoveryRSI的框架，它利用多智能体进化搜索和递归学习来生成可测试的科学假设。该框架通过构建假设树和执行可行的研究任务，提升假设的质量，并在生命科学基准测试中超越了基线代理。DiscoveryRSI通过三种机制进行自我改进，优化假设信用、识别有效策略和应用改进，从而不断提高研究效率。实验结果表明，经过自我改进后，假设质量显著提升，且在假设的重要性和可信度方面优于其他研究代理。

papers.title: Belief-Trajectory Energy: Measuring the Path to a Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract Belief-Trajectory Energy measures how inputs alter layerwise predictions in language models, yielding signals for task difficulty, review detection, and model attribution.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models (LLMs) progressively revise their predictions across Transformer layers, yet we typically observe only the final output, discarding the trajectory through which it is formed. We introduce Belief-Trajectory Energy(BTE), a model-grounded measure that characterizes an input through the layerwise predictive revisions it induces in a model. By mapping intermediate states into a shared predictive space, BTE provides a principled measure of belief change that can be summarized as either a scalar or a structured depth profile. Theoretically, we show that local BTE corresponds to predictive revision under the Fisher-Rao geometry, while the sequence of revisions captures information beyond the initial-to-final belief change. Empirically, scalar BTE provides a model-relative signal of difficulty across diverse reasoning tasks, while richer BTE representations support human-LLM review detection and fine-grained generator attribution, reaching up to 0.998 macro-AUROC and 95.6% eight-way attribution accuracy.
